subject: Multi-cloud SKU / packaging split proposal for initial listings
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Carter <alyssa@aws-marketplace.com>, Ben Strauss <ben.strauss@azure.com>, Priyanka Sharma <pri@gcp-partners.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud SKU / packaging split proposal for initial listings

Team & partners —

Attaching a first-pass SKU/packaging proposal for launching Redwood on AWS, Azure, and GCP marketplaces. High-level goals: 1) keep parity in billing units (vCPU-hours equivalent) across clouds, 2) minimize SKU proliferation so each cloud team can manage listings, 3) fast path a single "entry" SKU per cloud for region priority.

Notes in the attached spreadsheet (redwood_marketplace_sku_proposal_v1.xlsx) — key proposed items:
- Entry SKU: "Redwood Inference Starter" (single vCPU-equivalent, monthly subscription or pay-as-you-go listing depending on marketplace).
- Performance SKUs: Small / Medium / Large bundling by tokens-per-second and session concurrency; prefer 3 tiers rather than per-model SKUs.
- Regional gating: Launch US + EU first on AWS and Azure; GCP pilot focused on APAC later (regulatory checks pending).
- Packaging: Offer "hosted API" as default, "dedicated" as an add-on contract link (marketplace listing points to sales assist).

Questions I want us to resolve in this thread:
1) Are marketplaces okay with a single entry SKU that maps to multiple model variants behind the scenes (we do routing)?
2) Does anyone foresee regulatory or billing issues for our suggested EU-first parity?
3) Action items & owners for listing materials (T&Cs, marketing copy, pricing table).

Alyssa/Ben/Priyanka — if you can comment on constraints (SKU naming, required fields, billing granularity) that would be great.

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of GTM Partnerships (interim)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Multi-cloud SKU / packaging split proposal for initial listings

Thanks Rishi — good start. A few product and compliance flags from my side: 

- EU data residency: If we present an entry SKU that does not explicitly call out region enforcement, some customers will request region-pinned deployments. We should add an explicit field in the listing metadata indicating whether the SKU supports region pinning (yes/no) and what the default fallback is.

- Marketplace-specific packaging: Azure requires clearer meter definitions for compute vs. usage; a combined token-based metric may be problematic. Suggest we publish both a compute-metered and token-metered variant under the same offering where the marketplace supports multiple metering options.

- SKU count control: agree on 3 performance tiers + entry. But ask: for Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers, do we surface a separate "Enterprise Reserved" SKU or handle that off-marketplace via a procure link? My preference: off-marketplace for reserved capacity to avoid SKU sprawl and complex billing reconciliation.

Action proposals: 
- Marissa: draft marketplace copy + compliance blurb for EU data residency and region pinning (due EOD Thurs)
- Jonas: confirm B2B contract flow if we point "Reserved" to off-marketplace sales. Also confirm whether HubSpot records should be linked in listing as permitted.
- Rishi: follow up with marketplace reps on naming constraints (Alyssa/Ben/Priyanka).

On attachments: I added a short compliance checklist to the Drive folder (see related links).

Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Marketing

Subject: Re: Multi-cloud SKU / packaging split proposal for initial listings

Rishi/Soojin — thanks for sending this over. A few AWS Marketplace specifics: 

- Single entry SKU mapping: AWS allows you to use a single listing that maps to multiple fulfillment types, but you must declare the pricing dimensions up front. If you plan to route to different model variants, ensure the listing's description is explicit that customers may be routed to "equivalent" capacity tiers.

- Metering: We prefer discrete metering dimensions (e.g., vCPU-hours, instance-hours, or token-count). If you put both compute and token meters, make sure to clearly indicate the primary billing dimension to avoid billing disputes.

- Region defaults & data residency: You can include a region-pinning option, but if the customer selects a region at purchase, you must honor it (billing & delivery). Also, EU privacy teams sometimes require the listing to point to a data processing addendum — include the link to your DPA in the listing attachments.

- Marketplace integrations: Provide a single consolidated CSV for SKU -> price mapping per region; we'll ingest that to create pricing tables. For promotional/co-sell activities, provide a partner pitch deck and 3 customer case studies if you want us to prioritize co-sell introductions.

Happy to set up a short call with the SQL co-sell team next week if you want to discuss joint campaigns.

Best,
Alyssa Carter
AWS Marketplace — Partner Programs

- Dedicated/Reserved: Off-marketplace enterprise path with a clear link in the listing to contact sales / request a quote.
- EU handling: Add a checkbox in the checkout flow to opt into region-pinned deployments; link to our DPA.
